SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is early marriage harmful? (1 mark)
   A. It helps children learn
   B. It stops education and harms health
   C. It is fun
   D. It makes children rich

2. At what age can a person legally marry in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. 14 years
   B. 18 years
   C. 12 years
   D. 16 years

3. Which action helps a child with special needs? (1 mark)
   A. Including them in games
   B. Hiding them
   C. Laughing at them
   D. Neglecting them

4. What is female genital mutilation? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of school
   B. A kind of sport
   C. A kind of food
   D. Cutting a girl's private parts, which is harmful and illegal

5. What is child trafficking? (1 mark)
   A. Taking children on a picnic
   B. Taking children away by trick or force to make money from them
   C. Taking children to school
   D. Adopting children legally

6. Which shows respect for the minority? (1 mark)
   A. Listening to those who did not win
   B. Laughing at them
   C. Sending them away
   D. Ignoring them

7. What is a suggestion box used for? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping food
   B. Storing books
   C. Collecting rubbish
   D. Pupils drop ideas and complaints

8. What is a mock election? (1 mark)
   A. A game with no rules
   B. A school holiday
   C. A practice election
   D. A real national election

9. How many tally marks does a group of five look like? (1 mark)
   A. Four lines crossed by one line
   B. Two lines
   C. Six lines
   D. One line

10. What does democracy mean? (1 mark)
   A. Rule by one person
   B. Rule by force
   C. Rule by the people
   D. No rules

11. In a mock session, what should pupils do first after opening? (1 mark)
   A. Fight
   B. Leave
   C. Close the meeting
   D. Read the last minutes

12. Which shows respect for the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Insulting leaders
   B. Ignoring leaders
   C. Following fair instructions politely
   D. Laughing at them

13. What does a patron do? (1 mark)
   A. Cooks for pupils
   B. Drives the bus
   C. Guides and advises the pupil leaders
   D. Wins all elections

14. Which duty belongs to a religious leader? (1 mark)
   A. Selling goods
   B. Making laws
   C. Repairing cars
   D. Leading prayers and teaching values

15. How can you show respect for community leaders? (1 mark)
   A. Spread rumours
   B. Listen politely and follow fair rules
   C. Insult them
   D. Refuse to attend meetings

16. Which quality means not boasting or looking down on others? (1 mark)
   A. Humility
   B. Anger
   C. Pride
   D. Greed

17. Why do we have county governments? (1 mark)
   A. To stop elections
   B. To bring services closer to the people
   C. To end services
   D. To close schools

18. Which of these is a national government service? (1 mark)
   A. Pre-primary schools
   B. County markets
   C. Defence and security
   D. Cattle dips

19. What does the county executive do? (1 mark)
   A. Prints money
   B. Trains police
   C. Carries out the laws and runs county services
   D. Makes national laws

20. Which of these is a county government service? (1 mark)
   A. Running the army
   B. Issuing passports
   C. Running county health centres
   D. Defending the country

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. State three functions of the Children's Government. (3 marks)

22. Explain how a village elder can help two neighbours who quarrel about a fence. (4 marks)

23. Give four qualities of a good pupil leader. (4 marks)

24. Who is the patron of a Children's Government? (2 marks)

25. List four democratic processes in a school. (4 marks)

26. Explain why buying votes with sweets is wrong. (3 marks)

27. State three duties of the governor. (3 marks)

28. Give four duties of a religious leader. (4 marks)

29. Give three rules for using safe school transport. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — It stops education and harms health
   Early marriage harms girls and boys.

2. B — 18 years
   The law says a person must be 18 to marry.

3. A — Including them in games
   Children with special needs have equal rights.

4. D — Cutting a girl's private parts, which is harmful and illegal
   FGM harms girls and is against the law.

5. B — Taking children away by trick or force to make money from them
   Trafficking is a crime.

6. A — Listening to those who did not win
   Democracy includes everyone.

7. D — Pupils drop ideas and complaints
   It lets everyone share ideas.

8. C — A practice election
   A mock election teaches how voting works.

9. A — Four lines crossed by one line
   A group of five has four vertical lines and one crossing them.

10. C — Rule by the people
   Democracy means the people have a say.

11. D — Read the last minutes
   Minutes remind the group of past decisions.

12. C — Following fair instructions politely
   Respect includes obeying fair instructions.

13. C — Guides and advises the pupil leaders
   The patron is a teacher adviser.

14. D — Leading prayers and teaching values
   Religious leaders lead worship.

15. B — Listen politely and follow fair rules
   Respect means polite listening and obeying good rules.

16. A — Humility
   Humble leaders are modest.

17. B — To bring services closer to the people
   Counties bring services near to people.

18. C — Defence and security
   Defence is national.

19. C — Carries out the laws and runs county services
   The executive runs the county.

20. C — Running county health centres
   Health centres are a county responsibility.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Represent pupils, help keep order, and promote cleanliness. Accept organising activities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each function.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Listen to both, be fair, help them to talk and agree, and encourage them to forgive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Honest, fair, responsible and a good listener. Accept humble or hard working.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: The patron is a teacher who guides and advises the pupil leaders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a teacher, 1 mark for guides the pupil leaders.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Electing class monitors, class meetings, using a suggestion box, and voting on decisions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each process.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is cheating, it makes the election unfair, and votes should be given freely on merit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lead the county executive, present the budget and plans, and represent the county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: Lead prayers, teach values, counsel people and visit the sick. Accept conducting weddings or funerals.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use only transport approved by the school and parents, do not take lifts from strangers, and do not board overloaded vehicles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.
